# Design contract

Read before touching code. Supersedes the retired LEDGER contract (see `docs/adr/0005`).

## 0. Relationship to the Reference

dai.is-a.dev is the bar. We build in its idiom on purpose. Two rules govern what transfers:

**Adopt — the design language.** Dark-first with a real light theme. Geist Sans + Geist Mono. Small
type, tight tracking, generous line-height. Hairline borders instead of shadows. Quiet chrome that
never competes with content. Motion that is short, purposeful, and never decorative. A dense single
scroll on Home. A command palette as a craft signal. Pixel discipline everywhere.

**Do not adopt — the information architecture.** No component registry, no blocks, no sponsors, no
awards, no certifications, no testimonials, no bookmarks. Those sections work there because they are
full. We have four things worth showing and we show four things.

**Write our own code.** This is a rebuild in a shared idiom, not a fork and not a transcription. No
file is copied from the Reference. Its name, logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.

The failure mode to design against is not "looks similar" — it is **an impressive frame around thin
content**. Every section must be dense with real Proof or it does not exist.

## 1. Stack

Next.js (App Router) · React · TypeScript · Tailwind v4 · shadcn/ui on Radix + Base UI primitives ·
Motion for animation · `next-themes` · MDX via `next-mdx-remote` · Vercel. Latest stable at build
time. `bun` for everything.

## 2. Surfaces

```
/                 Masthead → AI Activity → Projects → footer      (single dense scroll)
/blog             hidden until the first real Post exists
/blog/[slug]      Post
/feed.xml         RSS                    ← survives from the old build
/writings         301 → /blog            ← survives from the old build
/og               dynamic OG images
/sitemap.xml /robots.txt
404
```

`rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.

## 3. Masthead

One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name · `agentic engineer` · one line of positioning · social links
(x · github · linkedin · email).

**The avatar slot is a designed absence.** No portrait exists yet. Reserve the exact final footprint
and render a bordered placeholder that carries the same cursor-tracking light interaction a real
photo would. Empty shape, live behaviour. Dropping in a portrait later must be a one-line change with
zero layout shift. It must never read as a broken image.

## 4. AI Activity

The density anchor and the largest element above the fold. A year grid of day cells, intensity by
token count, with a hover/focus readout carrying the exact value — the readout is a fixed line, not a
floating tooltip, so nothing reflows. Lifetime total set large.

- Server-rendered with the real total present in the HTML before hydration. No skeleton, no
  client-only fetch, no hydration mismatch.
- One SVG, not hundreds of nodes. Grid semantics with a per-cell accessible name.
- Full keyboard traversal; the readout is an `aria-live` region.
- Below the tablet breakpoint the grid re-orients to a month matrix rather than scrolling
  horizontally. Every cell has a ≥24×24 hit area.
- Fixture fallback renders identically and is labelled `fixture`. Data is never invented.

## 5. Projects

Eight, curated, in this order. Tier 1 is the agentic thesis; Tier 2 earns its place on shipped craft.

```
01  relunar     CLI repro harness for coding agents          relunar.com
02  pi-queue    FIFO queue and steering for pi               published on npm
03  offdex      Local-first Codex across phone, web, native
04  gunmetal    Local OpenAI-compatible API over your existing subscriptions
05  mdv-ts      Terminal markdown editor, TypeScript + OpenTUI
06  block       WebGPU generative logo explorer              live demo
07  codexchat   Subscription-backed inference chat, Rust
08  openutm-v0  Cross-platform UTM alternative
```

Rows, not cards — name, one line, language, year, outbound link. Hover reveals the destination host.
No thumbnails, no detail pages, no tag chips.

`pi-queue` shows **"published on npm"** as a fact and never a download counter — the real number is
too small to help. Revisit if relunar gains traction.

## 6. Type, colour, motion

**Type.** Geist Sans for language, Geist Mono for data and chrome (numbers, dates, labels, nav,
metadata, code). Tabular numerals globally — no number column ever reflows. Six sizes, no seventh.
Uppercase reserved for section labels only.

**Colour.** Dark is default and primary; light is a real design, not an inversion. Near-black rather
than pure black, near-white rather than pure white. One accent, used sparingly and enumerated in
code. Both themes must pass WCAG AA for all text; heatmap ramp steps below AA are never the sole
carrier of meaning — the readout always states the value.

**Motion.** Short and purposeful: hover ~150ms, entrance ~350ms, theme ~250ms. `Motion` is used only
where CSS genuinely cannot do the job. Nothing animates perpetually. Nothing parallaxes, pins, or
jacks the scroll. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes movement but keeps colour-only interaction
feedback.

## 7. Prohibitions

No empty sections. No placeholder or invented data. No "coming soon". No fake metrics. No box
shadows. No gradients except the heatmap ramp. No thumbnails or project detail pages. No hamburger
menu. No perpetual animation. No page-level fade on route change. No dashboard grammar.

## 8. Acceptance tests

1. `curl` of `/` contains the real lifetime token total; console shows no hydration mismatch.
2. At 1440×900 the masthead and the complete year grid are visible without scrolling.
3. Zero horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 2560.
4. Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390.
5. Full keyboard traversal of the heatmap, with the readout announced.
6. Both themes pass their stated contrast ratios.
7. Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical (no perpetual motion).
8. No section renders with zero real items — including Blog, which stays hidden at zero Posts.
9. Lighthouse: performance ≥95, accessibility 100, best practices 100, SEO 100. CLS = 0.
10. `/writings` still 301s to `/blog`; `/feed.xml` still validates.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

**23/100.** Ours copies Geist, thin rules, pills, and activity-grid vocabulary; it misses Chan Dai's actual frame system. Biggest failure: no bounded `md:max-w-3xl` rail scaffold, so every other cue floats as generic UI.

## THE 5 THINGS THAT MOST MAKE OURS LOOK FAKE

**1. Missing rail/grid scaffold**
- **His:** outer `max-w-screen overflow-x-clip px-2`; inner `mx-auto md:max-w-3xl`; `border-x border-line`; `screen-line-top/bottom` pseudo-rules spanning `left:-100vw; width:200vw; height:1px`
- **Ours:** `<main>` is `max-w-2xl px-5 sm:px-6`; no vertical rails, no viewport-spanning rules, no margin pattern
- **Consequence:** reads like centered Tailwind content, not his bounded instrument panel

**2. Wrong section grammar**
- **His:** every section is a `Panel` — `screen-line-top screen-line-bottom border-x border-line`; header `screen-line-bottom px-4`; title `font-heading text-3xl font-medium tracking-tight text-balance`
- **Ours:** `section-label` = mono 12px uppercase `.09em`; separate `.rule` at `mt-3`
- **Consequence:** generic dashboard label, not editorial panel architecture

**3. Typography numerically wrong**
- **His:** body `16px/1.5`; panel titles `30px/1.2` w500 `-.025em`; hero name `32px/1` w500; descriptions `15px/1.6`; nav `14px` w500 `.025em`. Loads Geist Sans, Geist Mono, IBM Plex Serif, Caveat
- **Ours:** body `15px/1.72`; hero name `17px/1.4`; labels `12px`; descriptions `13px/1.6`; no Caveat/Plex Serif
- **Consequence:** hierarchy collapses — small, airy, timid

**4. Color model wrong, not merely different**
- **His:** neutral zinc. Light `--background: oklch(1 0 0)`, dark `oklch(.141 .005 285.823)`, dark border `oklch(.274 .006 286.033)`, **neutral** `--accent`. Blue only for `--link`/`--info`

skills.name: caveman
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

Full from-scratch rebuild of dhruv2mars.com. Nothing is forked or transcribed from chanhdai.com — the design idiom is borrowed, the information architecture, copy, and data are ours.

## What changed

- **Retired the LEDGER contract.** `DESIGN.md` and `CONTEXT.md` rewritten from scratch; the LEDGER-era components, `lib/ledger.*`, `lib/home.*`, and the `/projects` route are gone.
- **New design system.** Rebuilt `app/globals.css` from zero: oklch tokens, a six-step type scale, hairline borders instead of shadows, tabular numerals, and CSS-only entrance animations that stop (no perpetual motion).
- **Home is a single dense scroll:** Masthead → AI Activity → Work → footer. Blog is the only sub-route.
- **Masthead** reserves the avatar footprint so dropping in a portrait later costs zero layout shift.
- **AI activity heatmap** redesigned as the density anchor: one column per week, fluid `aspect-ratio: 1` cells, a listbox with a single tab stop and arrow-key traversal, and a narrow-viewport window of 27 weeks derived from the real column count.
- **Work** is 8 curated projects.
- **Blog** is fully wired (MDX + RSS) but hidden until a real post exists, so no section renders empty.
- **Command palette** (⌘K), hand-rolled.

Three survivors were ported back unchanged: the `/writings → /blog` redirect, the feed/sitemap/robots routes, and the `rehype-sanitize` MDX hardening.

## Data honesty

The heatmap never invents activity. Gaps between the last published day and today are zero-filled so the series stays consecutive; today is projected — and drawn as a ring, not a fill — only when the feed published through yesterday. A stalled feed says so in the footer.

skills.name: caveman
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

skills.name: caveman
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. **Primary Request and Intent:** The user's current, active instruction (verbatim, their most recent substantive message): **"Do all of them, complete each and every part, including the polish and optional ones. Make sure that the entire website is fully done and done with other details. Once you are done, then use the same subagent workflow critic to do the review again. by comparing our version (draft pr preview in browser) and chan dai's site in browser, using computer use."** This means: implement **all 22 items** from the fidelity critic's plan (8 must-fix + 9 polish + 5 optional), then re-run the same Workflow-based critic — this time comparing the draft PR preview in a browser against dai.is-a.dev in a browser, using computer use (shelling out to `gpt-5.6-luna` via Codex per the global rule). skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

---
# Codex Computer Use

Delegate to Codex for verification needing real UI interaction, screenshots, simulator/browser state, or a runtime check outside this session. Skip this for code reading, linting, or tests you can run directly.

Ask first only if the run could disrupt the user's environment beyond the task itself (closing their apps, changing system settings, real accounts/data). Launching apps/simulators to verify your own work needs no confirmation.

## Run
```bash
ARTIFACT_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codex-computer-use.XXXXXX")"
PROMPT="$ARTIFACT_DIR/prompt.md"   # write the self-contained task here first
REPORT="$ARTIFACT_DIR/report.md"  # Codex writes its findings here

codex exec \
  -C "$PWD" --add-dir "$ARTIFACT_DIR" --skip-git-repo-check \
  -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=low \
  --yolo \
  -o "$REPORT" \
  "$(cat "$PROMPT")"
```
`--yolo` disables approval prompts and sandboxing — required for Codex to click, launch, and screenshot without stalling. Do not pair it with `--full-auto`; that silently downgrades the sandbox back to workspace-write. `-o` saves Codex's final write-up to `$REPORT` — read it back and relay pass/fail/blocked to the user.

## Prompt must include
Codex has no access to this conversation — the prompt file is everything it knows. Cover: exact behavior to verify; platform/app type; launch commands, creds, fixtures; edit permission (default: no source edits); where to save screenshots/logs; and require the reply state pass/fail/blocked + steps taken + observed behavior + screenshot paths + feedback.

# Task: side-by-side visual fidelity audit, in a real browser

You are auditing how closely a rebuilt personal portfolio matches the **design
idiom** of Chan Dai's site. You must do this with **computer use** — open both
sites in a real browser, look at them, scroll them, screenshot them, and
compare what you actually see. Do not audit from source code alone.

## The two sites

- **REFERENCE (the target idiom):** https://dai.is-a.dev/
- **OURS (the draft PR build):** try these in order, use the first that renders
  the page (not a login wall):
  1. https://dhruv2mars-git-feat-dai-idiom-rebuild-dhruv2mars.vercel.app/
     — this is the draft PR preview. It sits behind Vercel SSO. If the user's
     browser profile is already signed in to vercel.com it will load; if you
     land on a Vercel login screen, do NOT try to log in — fall back.
  2. http://localhost:3001/ — the identical production build of the same
     commit, served locally. Equivalent output; use it if (1) is gated.

State clearly in your report which of the two you actually used.

## Important framing — read this before judging

This is **not** a pixel-clone exercise, and marking it down for having
different content is wrong. Ours deliberately has:

- Its own information architecture. The owner has projects, an AI-token
  activity heatmap, and a blog that is intentionally hidden while it has zero
  posts. There is no components registry, no tech-stack grid, no experience
  timeline, no awards, no certifications — those sections do not exist because
  the proof behind them does not exist.
- No portrait photograph. The avatar slot renders a monogram plus a
  handwritten "portrait pending" margin note. That is a deliberate, honest
  placeholder, not an oversight.
- A stalled data feed on the heatmap, which the caption states honestly.

Judge **the idiom**: the frame system, density, rhythm, type, alignment,
restraint, and craft. Ask "would Chan Dai have built it this way?", not "does
it have the same sections?".

## What to compare, concretely

Go through these, on **both** sites, at **desktop width and mobile width**, and
in **both light and dark mode** (toggle the theme control in each site's
header):

1. **The frame.** Ruled hairlines that run edge to edge across the viewport;
   the vertical rails that bound the content column; where lines start and
   stop; whether anything floats free of the grid.
2. **Panels/sections.** Header composition (title, superscript count,
   description), inner padding, how a section separates from the next one
   (the diagonal-stripe bands).
3. **List rows.** Icon tile on the left, dashed inner rule, title/description
   stack, chip row, trailing affordance, hover treatment, row separators.
4. **Type.** Family pairing, sizes, weights, line-height, tracking, how
   monospace and tabular numerals are used, the small-caps/uppercase labels.
5. **Colour.** Neutral discipline. Background/foreground/muted relationships in
   both themes. Whether any accent hue leaks in where the reference is neutral.
6. **Spacing and density.** Vertical rhythm, whether ours feels emptier or
   looser than the reference, whether anything is orphaned in whitespace.
7. **Header and footer.** Sticky behaviour, control sizing and separators,
   footer composition.
8. **Interaction.** Hover states, focus rings (tab through), the command
   palette (press Cmd+K / Ctrl+K on ours), theme toggle, keyboard traversal of
   the heatmap (focus it, then arrow keys).
9. **Motion.** Whether anything loops or distracts. Reference and ours should
   both be calm.
10. **Craft slips.** Misaligned rules, double borders, off-by-one gaps,
    inconsistent radii, clipped text, layout shift, broken wrapping at
    narrow widths, contrast failures.

## Screenshots

Save every screenshot under `/tmp/critique/round2/` with descriptive names,
e.g. `ours-home-desktop-dark.png`, `dai-home-desktop-dark.png`. Capture at
minimum: home top, home mid-scroll, home bottom, and one mobile-width shot,
for each site, in each theme.

## Do not

- Do not edit any source files.
- Do not log in to anything.
- Do not fabricate observations you did not see on screen. If you could not
  check something (e.g. mobile width, or a theme), say so explicitly rather
  than guessing.

## Report format (write this to the output file)

```
VERDICT: <0-100> — how close ours is to Chan Dai's idiom
WHICH URL I USED: <preview | localhost:3001>, and why
WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: <list, or "nothing">

## Side-by-side observations
<for each of the 10 areas above: what the reference does, what ours does,
 and whether ours matches. Be specific — cite what you saw on screen.>

## Must-fix
<numbered. Each: what is wrong, where on the page, what it should be instead.
 Only things you actually observed.>

## Polish
<numbered, same format, lower severity.>

## What ours already gets right
<numbered. Be honest here too — do not pad.>

## Screenshots
<paths>
```

Be exacting and unsentimental. A high score must be earned.

# Task: side-by-side visual fidelity audit, in a real browser

You are auditing how closely a rebuilt personal portfolio matches the **design
idiom** of Chan Dai's site. You must do this with **computer use** — open both
sites in a real browser, look at them, scroll them, screenshot them, and
compare what you actually see. Do not audit from source code alone.

## The two sites

- **REFERENCE (the target idiom):** https://dai.is-a.dev/
- **OURS (the draft PR build):** try these in order, use the first that renders
  the page (not a login wall):
  1. https://dhruv2mars-git-feat-dai-idiom-rebuild-dhruv2mars.vercel.app/
     — this is the draft PR preview. It sits behind Vercel SSO. If the user's
     browser profile is already signed in to vercel.com it will load; if you
     land on a Vercel login screen, do NOT try to log in — fall back.
  2. http://localhost:3001/ — the identical production build of the same
     commit, served locally. Equivalent output; use it if (1) is gated.

State clearly in your report which of the two you actually used.

## Important framing — read this before judging

This is **not** a pixel-clone exercise, and marking it down for having
different content is wrong. Ours deliberately has:

- Its own information architecture. The owner has projects, an AI-token
  activity heatmap, and a blog that is intentionally hidden while it has zero
  posts. There is no components registry, no tech-stack grid, no experience
  timeline, no awards, no certifications — those sections do not exist because
  the proof behind them does not exist.
- No portrait photograph. The avatar slot renders a monogram plus a
  handwritten "portrait pending" margin note. That is a deliberate, honest
  placeholder, not an oversight.
- A stalled data feed on the heatmap, which the caption states honestly.

Judge **the idiom**: the frame system, density, rhythm, type, alignment,
restraint, and craft. Ask "would Chan Dai have built it this way?", not "does
it have the same sections?".

## What to compare, concretely

Go through these, on **both** sites, at **desktop width and mobile width**, and
in **both light and dark mode** (toggle the theme control in each site's
header):

1. **The frame.** Ruled hairlines that run edge to edge across the viewport;
   the vertical rails that bound the content column; where lines start and
   stop; whether anything floats free of the grid.
2. **Panels/sections.** Header composition (title, superscript count,
   description), inner padding, how a section separates from the next one
   (the diagonal-stripe bands).
3. **List rows.** Icon tile on the left, dashed inner rule, title/description
   stack, chip row, trailing affordance, hover treatment, row separators.
4. **Type.** Family pairing, sizes, weights, line-height, tracking, how
   monospace and tabular numerals are used, the small-caps/uppercase labels.
5. **Colour.** Neutral discipline. Background/foreground/muted relationships in
   both themes. Whether any accent hue leaks in where the reference is neutral.
6. **Spacing and density.** Vertical rhythm, whether ours feels emptier or
   looser than the reference, whether anything is orphaned in whitespace.
7. **Header and footer.** Sticky behaviour, control sizing and separators,
   footer composition.
8. **Interaction.** Hover states, focus rings (tab through), the command
   palette (press Cmd+K / Ctrl+K on ours), theme toggle, keyboard traversal of
   the heatmap (focus it, then arrow keys).
9. **Motion.** Whether anything loops or distracts. Reference and ours should
   both be calm.
10. **Craft slips.** Misaligned rules, double borders, off-by-one gaps,
    inconsistent radii, clipped text, layout shift, broken wrapping at
    narrow widths, contrast failures.

## Screenshots

Save every screenshot under `/tmp/critique/round2/` with descriptive names,
e.g. `ours-home-desktop-dark.png`, `dai-home-desktop-dark.png`. Capture at
minimum: home top, home mid-scroll, home bottom, and one mobile-width shot,
for each site, in each theme.

## Do not

- Do not edit any source files.
- Do not log in to anything.
- Do not fabricate observations you did not see on screen. If you could not
  check something (e.g. mobile width, or a theme), say so explicitly rather
  than guessing.

## Report format (write this to the output file)

```
VERDICT: <0-100> — how close ours is to Chan Dai's idiom
WHICH URL I USED: <preview | localhost:3001>, and why
WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: <list, or "nothing">

## Side-by-side observations
<for each of the 10 areas above: what the reference does, what ours does,
 and whether ours matches. Be specific — cite what you saw on screen.>

## Must-fix
<numbered. Each: what is wrong, where on the page, what it should be instead.
 Only things you actually observed.>

## Polish
<numbered, same format, lower severity.>

## What ours already gets right
<numbered. Be honest here too — do not pad.>

## Screenshots
<paths>
```

Be exacting and unsentimental. A high score must be earned.

skills.name: caveman
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)

1	VERDICT: 80/100 — strong frame-system and list-row match; hero construction, mobile overflow, and footer craft keep it from feeling fully Chan Dai.
2	WHICH URL I USED: localhost:3001, because the Vercel preview redirected to a Vercel login wall. I did not log in.
3	WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: Vercel preview equivalence (SSO blocked); reference heatmap keyboard traversal (its contribution graphic exposed no focusable grid/listbox semantics). Everything else below was checked in headed Chromium at 1440×900 and 390×844, light and dark.
4	
5	## Side-by-side observations
6	
7	1. **Frame** — Reference: 1px rules run viewport edge to edge; content rails sit around the centered column; hero adds diagonal perspective guides and hatched geometry; section separators use diagonal-stripe bands. Ours: same centered rails, full-width rules, and stripe separators in both themes. Ours hero cube floats on a mostly empty plane; diagonal/perspective construction does not continue through it. **Strong match, visible hero mismatch.**
8	
9	2. **Panels/sections** — Reference: section title + parenthetical count + copy-link affordance, restrained inner padding, then a single stripe band before the next panel. Ours: `AI activity` and `Projects` use the same count treatment and padding; `Fig. 2. feed stalled — last updated Jul 17` is honest; section bands align. Ours panel headers have fewer secondary controls and the footer transition shows two adjacent stripe bands. **Mostly matches; separator/footer transition needs cleanup.**
10	
11	3. **List rows** — Reference: left icon tile, dashed inner connector/rule, title/description stack, chip row, trailing chevron/link, ruled row separators; experience/project rows can expand. Ours project rows reproduce the icon tile, dashed vertical rule, stack, chips, trailing chain affordance, separators, and a subtle dark hover fill (`relunar` hover checked). Ours repeats one cube icon instead of reference's varied semantic icons and has no expand affordance because rows are direct project links. **Strong idiom match; repetition is a polish loss.**
12	
13	4. **Type** — Reference: Geist-like sans for UI/headings, monospace for metadata/chips/numerals, handwritten accent for notes/headings, careful small labels. Ours visibly uses the same sans/mono pairing, tabular-looking heatmap counts, uppercase-ish metadata labels, and handwritten `portrait pending` note. Ours project surface is more uniformly sans/mono; reference adds more serif/handwritten modulation in lower sections. **Strong match, slightly flatter type hierarchy.**
14	
15	5. **Colour** — Reference: disciplined neutral black/white/gray system; light theme uses hairline gray rules, dark theme uses near-black field; accent color does not leak into chrome. Ours follows the same neutral discipline in both themes; heatmap stays grayscale; the monogram placeholder does not inject an accent hue. **Match.**
16	
17	6. **Spacing and density** — Reference: dense, tightly ruled long page; compact rows and many small metadata blocks. Ours: top hero/description/social stack has more open vertical air; project rows remain compact and consistent, but the page ends much sooner and footer leaves broad empty fields. On 390px, the description wraps to three lines and pushes heatmap lower. **Good rhythm in rows; ours feels looser at hero/footer.**
18	
19	7. **Header and footer** — Reference: sticky ruled header; desktop nav and controls sit inside separators; mobile collapses nav to logo plus compact controls; footer uses denser ruled metadata/inspiration/legal composition plus geometric ornament. Ours: sticky desktop header and separators match; desktop controls are coherent. At 390px, `activity`, `work`, search, GitHub, and theme controls all remain in one row; the theme control is visibly clipped against the right scrollbar. Ours footer is a simple three-line metadata block plus icon row, not the reference's dense table-like composition. **Desktop match; mobile header is a must-fix, footer is under-crafted.**
20	
21	8. **Interaction** — Reference theme toggle changes the full neutral system; accordions and row affordances are calm. Ours theme toggle works in light/dark. `Control+K` opens a centered, blurred-background `Jump to…` palette with Home/Activity/Work, all projects, socials, RSS, and theme; Escape closes it. Heatmap focus works: listbox receives a visible 3px outline and ArrowRight/ArrowDown update `aria-activedescendant`. Ours project hover adds a restrained row fill. Reference heatmap did not expose a keyboard-focusable grid in the observed AX tree, so parity there could not be proven. **Ours interaction is strong and more semantically testable.**
22	
23	9. **Motion** — Reference remains calm; cursor/avatar-light notes add small, non-looping life. Ours cube/monogram/heatmap remain static; no distracting loop or attention capture observed. **Calm match; ours has less authored micro-life.**
24	
25	10. **Craft slips** — Reference rules, radii, and wrapping stayed consistent at inspected widths. Ours: clipped mobile theme control; horizontal scrollbar appears beneath the mobile heatmap; hero cube is visually disconnected from the frame's diagonal language; bottom project-to-footer transition shows two adjacent diagonal bands that read as a double border. No clipped desktop text or theme contrast failure observed. **Four concrete slips; first two are responsive defects.**
26	
27	## Must-fix
28	
29	1. At 390px, collapse or reflow the OURS header nav. `activity`/`work` plus search/GitHub/theme exceed the viewport; theme control is visibly cut off at right. Match reference mobile behavior: logo plus compact controls, no clipped control.
30	2. Remove mobile heatmap horizontal overflow. OURS shows a horizontal scrollbar under the grid at 390px; make cells/labels fit or provide intentional contained scrolling without page-level spill.
31	3. Reconnect hero art to frame language. Reference hero diagonals, rails, and hatched line-art form one construction; OURS solid cube floats centered in empty space. Carry ruled diagonals/hatched geometry through hero or otherwise anchor mark to rails.
32	4. Fix bottom separator composition. OURS shows two adjacent diagonal-stripe bands after the last project before footer; collapse to one intentional band or add a clearly purposeful gap/label.
33	
34	## Polish
35	
36	1. Add denser footer rhythm: ruled cells or aligned metadata columns, while keeping OURS's own content/IA. Current three-line block plus icon row feels sparse beside reference.
37	2. Vary project icon tiles or use semantic per-project marks. Repeated cube tile reads template-like beside reference's varied icon language.
38	3. Tune mobile hero density. Monogram tile is much smaller than reference portrait slot; keep the honest placeholder, but align its tile/title/subtitle proportions more deliberately.
39	4. Match desktop nav casing/weight more closely. OURS `activity`/`work` reads lighter and more lowercase than reference's compact title-case nav labels.
40	5. Normalize focus-ring treatment across header buttons, palette, links, and heatmap. Heatmap ring is clear; other controls are subtler and less obviously unified.
41	6. Restore a small authored micro-detail in hero or section notes. Reference's cursor/avatar-light annotations add personality without motion noise; OURS is appropriately calm but visually plainer.
42	
43	## What ours already gets right
44	
45	1. Centered content rails, edge-to-edge hairlines, and diagonal section bands line up with reference idiom at desktop and mobile.
46	2. Neutral light/dark palette stays disciplined; no stray accent color weakens the system.
47	3. Project rows have the right anatomy: icon tile, dashed inner rule, stack, chips, trailing affordance, separators, restrained hover.
48	4. Sans/mono pairing, small metadata labels, chip treatment, and count numerals feel intentionally designed rather than default browser UI.
49	5. Sticky header, theme toggle, command palette, Escape close, focus ring, and heatmap arrow traversal all worked in the rendered build.
50	6. Truthful product choices read as craft: monogram + `portrait pending`, intentionally hidden empty blog, and `feed stalled` caption do not pretend to have proof that is absent.
51	7. Motion stays quiet. Page does not loop, pulse, or distract while scrolling.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

skills.name: caveman
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/dhruv2mars/.claude/skills/caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.
